I assume objects, but we want to be 100% sure 🙂 cc: <@912415191067676693> <@792822129019584562> cc <@308223150725005322> the format in the engine api is the “json rpc” format we use in that context so the EL will receive the data as an array of withdrawals where each field is listed separately in the json syntax when making an execution block as regards consensus, the withdrawals are RLP encoded just like transactions (and the rest of the block) this mirrors the current usage of the engine api while retaining backwards compatibility with the EL the transactions in the engine api are a bit of a special case and really just bc we kept them “opaque” to the CL — we can (and should imo) change this in the future no reason i can see to do the same with the withdrawals here, as the reasoning for txns was mainly to avoid making the decision on ssz vs rlp boundary decision okay thx! 🙂 the format in the engine api is the yes i got confused as well when i was tryying interop with <@360491619402776577> 's build, and post using this object format it went through One of the nice things that happened with being bought by offchainlabs is that there's weekly shout-outs to acknowledge any achievement of members that you want to publicly recognize. excerpts.author: marekm3498
excerpts.content:
<@539495253418180618> I have a quick question about withdrawals in newPayload. In engine spec we have:
"- `withdrawals`: `Array of WithdrawalV1` - Array of withdrawals, each object is an `OBJECT` containing the fields of a `WithdrawalV1` structure." https://github.com/ralexstokes/execution-apis/blob/add-withdrawal-operations/src/engine/specification.md#executionpayloadv2

However, in EIP-4895 we have:
"The execution payload gains a new field for the withdrawals which is an RLP list of Withdrawal data."
https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4895#new-field-in-the-execution-payload-withdrawals

Should EL expect objects or rlp enoded array (like transactions)? I assume objects, but we want to be 100% sure 🙂 
cc: <@912415191067676693> <@792822129019584562>

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
the format in the engine api is the “json rpc” format we use in that context 

so the EL will receive the data as an array of withdrawals where each field is listed separately in the json syntax 

when making an execution block as regards consensus, the withdrawals are RLP encoded just like transactions (and the rest of the block)

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: this mirrors the current usage of the engine api while retaining backwards compatibility with the EL

excerpts.content: no reason i can see to do the same with the withdrawals here, as the reasoning for txns was mainly to avoid making the decision on ssz vs rlp boundary decision
